title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Ten admission-free outings at Calvin University and public splash pads around Grand Rapids, with current access details from university and city sources.

cards.title: Walk the Preserve Trails Together
cards.subtitle: A free public trail hang on Calvin’s east campus
cards.notes: Meet at the main entrance, follow the marked walking trails, and keep the outing low-impact by staying out of ponds and wildlife areas.
cards.short_summary: Take an unhurried group walk through publicly accessible forest, meadow, and wetland habitat.
cards.evidence_claim: Calvin states that the preserve’s walking trails are open to the public for free every day from 7 a.m. until dusk.
cards.access_notes: Public daily from 7 a.m. to dusk. Hiking only; stay on trails. No running, biking, dogs, alcohol, fishing, or entry into water bodies.

cards.title: Explore the Bunker Interpretive Center
cards.subtitle: A free indoor meet-up beside Calvin’s preserve
cards.notes: Gather inside to examine the environmental displays, then continue onto the preserve trails while the center and paths are open.
cards.short_summary: Pair an indoor nature-learning stop with conversation before or after a preserve walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Calvin identifies the Bunker Interpretive Center as part of the preserve and states that admission to the center is free.
cards.access_notes: Free admission. Open Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m. in summer and 9 a.m.–5 p.m. during the academic year; closed weekends and listed holidays.

cards.title: Compare Minerals at the Dice Museum
cards.subtitle: A free geological collection on Calvin’s campus
cards.notes: Bring a friend and compare the fluorescent minerals, fossils, meteorites, native copper, and other specimens in the rotating collection.
cards.short_summary: Browse hundreds of geological specimens and trade observations without buying a ticket.
cards.evidence_claim: Calvin says visitors may browse the Bruce Dice Mineralogical Museum independently or take a tour free of charge.
cards.source_title: Bruce Dice Mineralogical Museum | Calvin University
cards.access_notes: Admission is free. For August 2026, the museum lists weekday hours of 1–4 p.m. from August 3–28; confirm later academic-year hours before visiting.

cards.title: Cool Off at Alger Park
cards.subtitle: Free seasonal water play south of Calvin
cards.notes: Coordinate towels and sun protection, meet by the splash pad, and activate the water features with a bare hand or foot on the sensors.
cards.short_summary: Turn a warm afternoon into a casual, admission-free splash-pad meet-up.
cards.evidence_claim: Grand Rapids lists Alger Park Splash Pad among its city splash pads and states that splash-pad admission is free.
cards.source_title: Pools and Splashpads | City of Grand Rapids
cards.access_notes: Free admission. The 2026 season runs June 6–September 13, with daily hours of 10 a.m.–9 p.m. Located at 921 Alger St SE.

cards.title: Take a Splash Break at Aberdeen
cards.subtitle: A no-ticket summer hang in northeast Grand Rapids
cards.notes: Pick a warm day, pack water and towels, and use the sensor-operated splash features for an easy group break with no admission charge.
cards.short_summary: Meet for free outdoor water play during the city’s published summer season.
cards.evidence_claim: Grand Rapids names Aberdeen Park Splash Pad as a city splash-pad location and explicitly lists splash-pad admission as free.
cards.source_title: Pools and Splashpads | City of Grand Rapids
cards.access_notes: Free admission. The 2026 season runs June 6–September 13, with daily hours of 10 a.m.–9 p.m. Located at 2230 Eastern Ave NE.

cards.title: Meet Up at Cherry Park’s Splash Pad
cards.subtitle: Free seasonal water features near central Grand Rapids
cards.notes: Plan a daytime group stop, bring quick-drying clothes, and activate the splash-pad sensors without needing tickets or a purchase.
cards.short_summary: Share a simple warm-weather outing at a city-operated splash pad with free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Grand Rapids includes Cherry Park Splash Pad in its official list and states that admission to city splash pads is free.
cards.source_title: Pools and Splashpads | City of Grand Rapids
cards.access_notes: Free admission. The 2026 season runs June 6–September 13, with daily hours of 10 a.m.–9 p.m. Located at 725 Cherry St SE.

cards.title: Reset at Fuller Park
cards.subtitle: A free splash-pad outing on Fuller Avenue
cards.notes: Invite a few friends for a short cooldown, use the touch sensors to start the water, and bring everything needed for a comfortable visit.
cards.short_summary: Add a playful, cost-free water stop to a summer afternoon in the city.
cards.evidence_claim: Grand Rapids lists Fuller Park Splash Pad at 250 Fuller Avenue NE and identifies admission to its splash pads as free.
cards.source_title: Pools and Splashpads | City of Grand Rapids
cards.access_notes: Free admission. The 2026 season runs June 6–September 13, with daily hours of 10 a.m.–9 p.m. Located at 250 Fuller Ave NE.

cards.title: Gather at Garfield Park’s Splash Pad
cards.subtitle: Free outdoor water play in southeast Grand Rapids
cards.notes: Set a meeting time near the splash area, carry towels and sunscreen, and enjoy the sensor-activated features during posted seasonal hours.
cards.short_summary: Use the city’s free splash pad as the centerpiece of a relaxed group outing.
cards.evidence_claim: The city’s official splash-pad page names Garfield Park Splash Pad and says admission to all listed splash pads is free.
cards.source_title: Pools and Splashpads | City of Grand Rapids
cards.access_notes: Free admission. The 2026 season runs June 6–September 13, with daily hours of 10 a.m.–9 p.m. Located at 2111 Madison Ave SE.

cards.title: Beat the Heat at Highland Park
cards.subtitle: A free summer splash stop north of downtown
cards.notes: Choose a sunny afternoon, bring refillable water bottles and towels, and meet at the splash pad for a purchase-free group cooldown.
cards.short_summary: Cool down together at a named public splash pad with no admission requirement.
cards.evidence_claim: Grand Rapids identifies Highland Park Splash Pad as one of its 15 locations and states that splash-pad admission is free.
cards.source_title: Pools and Splashpads | City of Grand Rapids
cards.access_notes: Free admission. The 2026 season runs June 6–September 13, with daily hours of 10 a.m.–9 p.m. Located at 700 College Ave NE.

cards.subtitle: Free warm-weather water play in southeast Grand Rapids
cards.notes: Round up friends, pack towels and sun protection, and use the city’s sensor-operated water features during the published season.
cards.short_summary: Make an easy social afternoon around free, city-maintained splash features.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Grand Rapids lists Joe Taylor Park Splash Pad and explicitly states that admission to city splash pads is free.
